Ported from commit 98188486ccda7e0303faae544eab5cb32f36772f of the unified-core branch test/decoder-core-unification-20261104. ARM experience follows the previous M4 experiment (538faeca1595eb164ef3e02e7b60108452436596). This round first produced M4 parent e18618a53c5493154d307bf46684599e3bbab9bc, then adopted the consecutive-component implementation 631202519ea2805368774442c9cd03eb93b9e6ed. The primary performance denominator is unmodified official PyMatching v2.3.1: e27b8c6a5f5ba10fb74d4ebb29822f2df5e12bcd.

Adopted optimizations

  • Moved ARM/Darwin support into the unified core, retaining structured scalar matching. NEON handles predecoder caps and minimum-edge-weight reductions; the fused Bound kernel is selected during construction. The actual low-syndrome serial fallback remains, with a Spatial component threshold of 32.
  • Each TailReset or Spatial X/Z component or component group completes prepare, MWPM and extraction consecutively, followed by waiting and merging. Solving one group can overlap preparation of another. Double-buffer cleanup across shots, existing test fixes and build settings remain.
  • In paired 10,000-shot exploratory measurements, the equal-weight geometric means over 21 settings of parent latency / new latency were 1.0387x for TailReset and 1.0629x for Spatial. The change was adopted after one confirmation under the frozen rule. Records for seven settings with unstable directions remain; no claim of stable improvement at every point is made.

Million-shot horizontal ablation

Apple M4 Pro, seven code distances and three error rates, with one million saved independent inputs per setting. The primary value is the median of three complete-batch means per shot. Speedup is official latency / current latency for the same setting, followed by the equal-weight geometric mean over 21 settings. The first four columns reuse the original measurement window; TailReset and Spatial use new supplementary measurements. Comparisons across windows are descriptive.

New TailReset and Spatial achieve 1.0241x and 1.0317x relative to the previous versions of the same roles; these are observations across measurement windows. Adjacent ablation ratios remain 0.9701x for Component to TailReset and 0.9052x for TailReset to Spatial; all observed regressions are retained. Spatial at d=9, p=0.05% is about 7.56% slower than its previous version. Formal measurements were not used for retuning.

Per-shot latency tail distribution (CCDF)

The main figure uses the largest code distance in this round, d=33, with three horizontal panels for p=0.05%, 0.1% and 0.3%. It compares official PyMatching with five M4 ablation configurations. The horizontal axis is the linear latency threshold t (microseconds); the vertical axis is the strict exceedance probability P(L>t) on a logarithmic scale. At the same threshold, a lower curve means fewer shots exceed that latency.

At d=33, p=0.3%, the p99 latencies of official PyMatching, TailReset and Spatial are 421.666, 112.167 and 107.458 microseconds. These are measured latencies on the same saved inputs. The first four configurations reuse earlier measurements, while TailReset and Spatial use supplementary measurements after consecutive component execution. Cross-window comparisons remain descriptive.

Each curve comes from one per-shot measurement pass, with empirical resolution 10^-6, or one observation. Extreme-tail support is limited; no exponential fit or extrapolation to smaller probabilities is used. Per-shot timing includes decoding and result storage; drain at the end of each chunk is recorded separately. Clock-reading overhead remains. The complete PDF below covers seven distances and 21 settings, with three horizontal panels per page.

Validation and reproduction limits

The additional 168 million-shot execution audits found no weight differences. Eight observable differences came from the same original input; the actual matching edges from the new implementation were checked for syndrome parity and equal weight with the official result. Across 48 complete histories, each of the actual-matching and stage-recording phases joined 48 million outputs. All 362 witnesses, 724 component records and 362 original-shot latency-cleanup checks passed. Full ASan/UBSan: 330 passed and one x86-specific test skipped; seven auxiliary tests passed. The preset builds and all 600 CLI output checks across six roles passed.

Timing retains dispatch, waiting, merging, result storage and final drain; it excludes model construction, I/O, warmup and team startup/exit. Per-shot latency is collected separately; overlapping stages are not summed into wall-time shares. QoS and CPU time are recorded, but Darwin physical P/E-core affinity is unverified. Busy-wait CPU time is not separated from useful computation. Full Python, TSan and LSan validation were not rerun for the new source; prior Python results retain their parent identity. A new test directly establishes that MWPM can finish before another group completes preparation, but extraction overlap duration was not quantified separately.

Figure PDFs and per-setting results:

The complete technical and reproduction package contains final figures and plotting data, frozen protocols, per-setting and per-repeat results, latency and fixed-case tables, key C++ code with line-by-line explanations in the original language, actual assembly and validation receipts. Large raw runs and binaries remain in the local formal-artifact directory; the package records paths and SHA256 values. See SNAPSHOT.json for the snapshot scope.
